                    ### Question
                    Which of the following morphological features do we expect to find in the biopsy of the gastric body of a patient with vitamin B12 deficiency?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Helicobacter pylori.
opb. Intestinal metaplasia
opc. Hyperplasia of endocrine cells.
opd. Atrophy.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Vitamin B12 deficiency is associated with atrophic gastritis, which leads to atrophy of the gastric mucosa. This is due to impaired DNA synthesis and chronic inflammation, which can also predispose to intestinal metaplasia. While Helicobacter pylori may be present in some cases of chronic gastritis, it is not a direct consequence of vitamin B12 deficiency itself. Hyperplasia of endocrine cells can occur as a compensatory response to low intrinsic factor, but it is less commonly emphasized in the context of vitamin B12 deficiency compared to atrophy. Therefore, the most expected morphological feature in the biopsy of the gastric body of a patient with vitamin B12 deficiency is atrophy.
